items.title: Negativity of contracted curves on regular surfaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the Euler-characteristic and intersection suppliers. Let $k$ be a
field, let $X$ be an integral regular projective surface over $k$
([[def-divisor-intersection-number-on-smooth-projective-surface]]), let $Y$ be an integral regular finite-type
$k$-scheme of pure dimension two, let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a proper birational morphism and let $E\subseteq X$
be an integral curve with $f(E)$ a single closed point $y\in Y$. Then:

1. $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$;
2. $\deg_E\bigl(\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E\bigr)>0$, that is, the conormal sheaf of $E$ in $X$ has positive degree on $E$; and
3. $E\cdot E<0$; equivalently the normal bundle $\mathcal O_X(E)|_E$ has negative degree.

No similar statement is proved here for curves not contracted by a birational morphism, and no negative definiteness of the full intersection matrix of a reducible exceptional divisor is claimed.
items.strategy: At every point of $X$ the local ring is a regular local ring, hence a UFD ([[thm-nonaffine-regular-local-ring-is-ufd]]); the height-one prime defining the integral curve $E$ is therefore locally principal, so $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor. This proves (1). Part (2) is [[lem-positive-conormal-degree-of-a-fibre-divisor]] applied to $Z=E$, whose only component is $E$; note $E\subseteq f^{-1}(y)$ set-theoretically. For (3) use $E\cdot E=\deg_E\mathcal O_X(E)|_E$ ([[thm-intersection-with-curve-as-degree-of-restriction]]) and additivity of degrees on inverse bundles ([[cor-degree-additive-proper-curve]]): $\deg_E\mathcal O_X(E)|_E+\deg_E\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E=0$, so (2) gives $E\cdot E<0$.

items.title: Dualizing modules and trace pairing for normal projective surface modifications
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $R$ be a regular Noetherian local ring of dimension two, let $A$ be a finite normal local $R$-domain of dimension two, with $R\hookrightarrow A$ local, and let $X$ be a normal integral scheme of dimension two projective over $R$, with a proper birational map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Put $\omega_A=\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,R)$. The regular-base projective dualizing complex is canonically $D_X=\omega_X[2]$ with $\omega_X$ a coherent CM torsion-free module of generic rank one, and $D_A=\omega_A[2]$. Evaluation gives $R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\omega_A)$. Its trace to $\omega_A$ is the dual of $A\to R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$; these are pairings of complexes with their natural $A$-actions.
items.strategy: Normality's S2 condition makes all local rings of $A$ and $X$ CM, since their dimensions are at most two. A regular parameter pair of $R$ generates an ideal primary to the maximal ideal of the finite local algebra $A$, so is a system of parameters there and is $A$-regular. Thus $\operatorname{depth}_R A=2$ and Auslander–Buchsbaum makes $A$ finite free over $R$. Hence the finite-base dualizing complex is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,R)[2]$. Fix a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P_R^N$. At a closed point, properness puts the image in the closed fibre and its residue field is finite over that of $R$. The ambient polynomial local ring has dimension $N+2$: its parameter pair from $R$ is regular and quotienting gives the $N$-dimensional regular polynomial local ring over the residue field. Its prime ideal defining the integral affine chart of $X$ has height $N$: it avoids nonzero $R$-elements and localization to $\operatorname{Frac}R$ gives a polynomial ring in $N$ variables modulo a prime with finite residue field extension (the generic field of $X$ is finite over $\operatorname{Frac}R$). Chains below that prime all avoid the same multiplicative set, so their heights are unchanged. The preceding CM dimension formula gives local dimension two on $X$, and Ext concentration gives $D_X$ only in degree $-2$ at this closed point. Every point of the proper Noetherian scheme specializes to a closed point, so coherent cohomology sheaves vanish globally outside that degree. The same Ext argument makes $\omega_X$ CM with full support. The full-dimension associated-prime property on its local CM stalks makes it torsion-free on the normal integral surface. At the generic point homothety identifies its endomorphisms with the function field, so its finite-dimensional generic vector space has rank one. The projective regular-base complex duality applied to $K=\mathcal O_X$, followed by finite-ring coinduction and cancellation of the common shift two, gives the displayed quasi-isomorphism. All arrows are evaluation/coinduction pairings, so the induced trace is exactly dual to the unit on structure-sheaf cohomology and is $A$-linear. No smoothness, perfect ground field, or general proper f-shriek theorem was imported.

items.title: Positive conormal degree for a fibre divisor on a normal surface
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal Noetherian local domain of dimension two and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a normal integral modification. For any nonempty effective Cartier divisor $Z$ supported in the special fibre, some integral component $C$ of $Z$ satisfies $\deg_C(\mathcal O_X(-Z)|_C)>0$. In particular its conormal bundle is not trivial.
items.strategy: Write the one-dimensional fibre components $C_j$ and choose closed points $x_j$ off all other components. Such points exist in the nonempty open of each finite-type proper residue-field curve. Choose $g_j\in\mathfrak m_{X,x_j}$ with nonzero image in $\mathcal O_{C_j,x_j}$. In the common function field write $g_j=a_j/b_j$ with $a_j,b_j\in A$ and set $u=\prod a_j$. Each $a_j$ lies in the maximal ideal: otherwise $g_jb_j=a_j$ would make $g_j$ a unit. Thus $u$ has positive orders $e_j$ at the generic DVRs of all fibre curves, and $u=g_jh_j$ locally at $x_j$. Put $d_j=v_{C_j}(Z)$. Choose $i$ maximizing $d_i/e_i$ and rescale $u\mapsto u^{d_i}$, $Z\mapsto e_iZ$. The new orders satisfy $v_{C_j}(u)\ge v_{C_j}(Z)$ for all $j$, with equality at $i$. Normal surface local rings are CM; their effective Cartier quotients are CM, because a nonzerodivisor extends to a parameter tuple by the support-dimension argument, and hence have no embedded associated points. The image of $u$ in $\mathcal O_Z$ is zero at every generic associated point, hence zero, so $u$ is a section of the Cartier ideal $I$. Its restriction to $C_i$ is nonzero generically by equality of orders. Near $x_i$ only $C_i$ occurs in $Z$; the factor $g_i$ (raised to the rescaling power if necessary) is nonzero at its sole associated generic point, so is a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_Z$. If $I=(t)$, $g_ih_i\in(t)$ therefore implies $h_i\in(t)$. Thus $u/t=g_i(h_i/t)$ vanishes at $x_i$. The corrected proper-integral-curve section/degree lemma gives positive degree. Tensor-power additivity removes the positive rescaling factor. This proves the normal-surface version; the original regular-surface helper was not silently applied outside its Statement.

items.title: The Leray sequence for normal surface modifications
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal local domain of dimension two in the field/complete-equicharacteristic finite-type class, and $X'\xrightarrow gX\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ normal integral modifications. Then $g_*\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal O_X$ and $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^1(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ is injective. If $X$ is projective over $A$, there is a natural exact sequence $0\to H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^1(X',\mathcal O_{X'})\to H^0(X,R^1g_*\mathcal O_{X'})\to0$. The last sheaf is coherent, supported on finitely many closed points and generated by global sections.
items.strategy: On each affine normal target chart, proper coherent pushforward gives a finite algebra contained in the common function field; its elements are integral over the chart and hence lie in that normal chart. This proves g*O=O. The degree-one Leray five-term sequence then supplies the injection, without requiring projectivity of either scheme. The codimension-one isomorphism helper says g is an isomorphism off finitely many closed points of X. R1g*O is coherent by proper coherent finiteness and vanishes on that isomorphism open. A coherent sheaf supported on finitely many closed points is a pushforward from a finite zero-dimensional closed subscheme: a power of its radical annihilator annihilates the sheaf, whose coordinate rings are Artinian. Such a subscheme is a finite disjoint union of affine local Artinian schemes, so its finite modules are generated by their global sections and have no higher cohomology. If X is projective its two-affine cover makes H2(X,O)=0, so the next term of the five-term sequence vanishes and gives the short exact sequence. Localization/flat Čech comparison identifies the stalk at a closed point x with H1 of the localized modification over O_X,x.

items.title: A nonsingular formal arc on a normal Noetherian surface becomes regular
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal Noetherian local domain of dimension two with a surjection onto a complete DVR $V$ inducing its residue-field identification. The successive point blowups along this nonsingular arc become regular at the arc centre after finitely many steps.
items.strategy: Let P=ker(A→V), choose t mapping to a V-uniformizer, and minimally generate P by u2,...,ur. Then m=(t,u2,...,ur). The CM dimension formula makes P height one, so A_P is a DVR. Since a generator of its maximal ideal must occur among the ui, relabel so u2 is a uniformizer there. The finite module P/(P²+(u2)) vanishes at P; as a finite module over A/P=V it is torsion, hence killed by a power of t. Thus for i>2 choose ni≥0 and ai∈A with t^ni ui−ai u2∈P². If ni=0, modulo mP this removes ui from the minimal generating family. If ai is a unit, it removes u2 instead. Otherwise ai mod P is either zero or a unit times t^mi with mi>0; absorb its P part into P². When all ni>0 and relevant mi>0, on the arc's t-chart set vi=ui/t. Dividing the relations by t² gives t^(ni−1)vi−unit·t^(mi−1)v2 in (v2,...,vr)², or t^(ni−1)vi in that square. Localize at the arc centre; the kernel of its surjection to V is generated by the vi and t remains a uniformizer. If the minimal number of generators drops, restart with that smaller number; its height-one localization is still A_P, since t is outside P and the blowups are isomorphisms there. Otherwise the displayed nonnegative exponents decrease at every step until one becomes zero, forcing a generator drop by Nakayama. There can only be finitely many drops. At the end P has one generator and m is generated by two elements; the local domain has dimension two by the modification dimension helper, hence is regular. This supplies the finite decreasing-invariant argument behind the source's short final paragraph.

items.title: Surface completed polynomial generic fibre
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $A$ be a complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local domain, let $\mathfrak q$ be maximal in $A[t]$ over its closed point, and let $0\ne\mathfrak r\subset\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal with $\mathfrak r\cap A=0$. Then $\widehat{A[t]_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes_{A[t]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.
items.strategy: The field κ(r) is finite over K=Frac(A). For every finite purely inseparable L/κ(r), choose finite A⊂A′⊂L with Frac(A′)=L. Since A′ is a complete local domain (finite algebra over complete local A, and a domain), finite completion factors reduce the problem to the case κ(r)=Frac(A). In that case rK[t]=(t-f), f∈K. Put T=A[t]_q^hat⊗_A K. Need T geometrically regular over K. Reduce first to a finite regular power-series subring A0 of A, and to factors of the finite base change of its completed polynomial local ring B0. B0 is regular, since A0[t]_q0 is regular. To prove B0⊗K0 geometrically regular in characteristic p, induct on finite purely inseparable extensions as in the generic-power-series lemma. For finite A0⊂A1⊂M, apply finite-completion factors to A0[t]⊂A1[t]: B0⊗A0 A1 is exactly the product of the local completions of A1[t] at primes over q0. Extend the detecting derivation of A1 coefficientwise to A1[t], fixing t, and then by the already proved localization/completion formulas to every factor. Taking their product gives a derivation on B0⊗A0 A1, and localizing gives one on B0⊗K0 M. Its value D(f) lies in M×. The hypersurface argument closes each degree-p step. The completion formula uses the q0-adic topology, which is equivalent on every finite factor to its maximal-adic topology; no formal-smooth lifting or André theorem is used. In characteristic zero separable extensions suffice. Thus T is regular; ∂/∂t extends to T and sends t-f to 1, so the hypersurface lemma proves T/(t-f) regular. The argument also applies after the finite A′ reduction and hence gives geometric regularity. items.title: Surface finite type formal fibres
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a field or a complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local ring and $B$ an essentially finite-type $A$-algebra. Every formal fibre of every local ring of $B$ is geometrically regular over its residue fraction field. Equivalently, for primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $B$, $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is geometrically regular.
items.strategy: A field is a complete local ring. A quotient has the property by completion/quotient compatibility. Reduce finite-type algebras to polynomial rings and induct on the number of variables. For the one-variable step, check local rings at maximal primes q. Put p=q∩R, localize R at p, and base change to its completion. The resulting completed polynomial local ring has the same completion as R[t]_q, as is seen modulo each power of q. Base change of R_p→R_p^hat is regular, and the preceding two fibre lemmas cover respectively the zero and nonzero generic primes after quotienting the complete base by their contraction. Thus the polynomial completion map is regular by composition and faithfully flat descent. To pass from maximal primes to all primes, choose P′ above P in R_m^hat, complete at P′, and use the complete-ring formal-fibre result and faithfully flat descent for R_P^hat→(R_m^hat)_(P′)^hat. Flatness here is the completion/base-change flatness; fibres descend because regularity descends along faithfully flat local maps. These are substantive permanence facts, not an inference from a graph. The map between completions in the maximal-prime reduction is flat, by the following direct argument. For a flat local R→S, choose a degreewise finite free resolution of its residue field over R. Tensoring with S is exact in positive degrees; complete those finite S-modules, using exactness of completion, and identify the complex with its tensor over R^hat with S^hat. This gives Tor_1^(R^hat)(k,S^hat)=0. Apply the published lem-ag-local-flatness-regular-parameters, whose first assertion allows a finite S^hat-module without requiring finiteness over R^hat. Locality then gives faithful flatness. In the polynomial step R[t]_q^hat and (R^hat[t]_q′)^hat are actually isomorphic: modulo q^n the coefficients are unchanged since m^n⊂q^n, and localization commutes with this comparison. Composition/base change of regular maps is checked fibrewise using flat-local ascent, after each finite field extension; faithful-flat descent uses the descent clause of lem-flat-local-ascent-of-regularity at each prime. No universal catenarity is used. Exact source/proof evidence is retained in the normal-completion-sources helper packet; AC and DC inherited from the used suppliers are explicit.

items.title: Surface regular fibres preserve normality
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. A flat map of Noetherian rings with regular fibres carries normality of the base to normality of the target. Consequently a normal essentially finite-type local ring over a field or complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local base has normal maximal-adic completion, which is a domain.
items.strategy: At S_Q over R_P the published flat-local depth formula and the inequality dim(S_Q)≤dim(R_P)+dim(fibre) prove S2: the inequality follows by lifting a system of parameters from the base and fibre, which together generate an ideal primary for the maximal ideal. For height≤1 in S, going down bounds dim(R_P)≤1, and the fibre is a quotient of S_Q so also has dimension≤1; base and fibre are regular. Lift their regular systems of parameters. The published sequence-lifting lemma makes their concatenation regular; they generate the maximal ideal, so depth≤dimension≤embedding dimension forces regularity. Thus S is S2 and R1. For completeness, the domain-only published Serre criterion is not enough. An S2 ring is S1, hence has no embedded associated primes; with R0 it is reduced, by injecting into localizations at its minimal associated primes, all fields. Let t∈Q(S) be integral. It lies in every height≤1 localization, since they are regular local domains. Put I={a∈S:at∈S}. If proper, choose a prime minimal over I, of height≥2, and localize there. The localized I is primary for the maximal ideal; S2 supplies an S-regular sequence x,y in I by prime avoidance. From y(xt)=x(yt), regularity modulo x gives xt∈xS, and cancellation gives t∈S, contradiction. Hence S is integrally closed in Q(S). The idempotents of Q(S), one per minimal component, are integral and belong to S, so a local such S has only one component and is a domain. Apply this to the completion map using the preceding formal-fibre lemma and published faithful flatness. For the denominator-ideal regular sequence, in the localization at a minimal prime over I one has sqrt(I)=m. Depth≥2 means m is contained in no associated prime of S, so I is contained in none either. Finite prime avoidance chooses a nonzerodivisor x∈I. Depth(S/xS)≥1 similarly chooses y∈I nonzerodivisor modulo x. This proves the required sequence in I. At all height-one primes Q(S) localizes into the fraction field of S_Q: a global nonzerodivisor remains one under localization. items.title: Surface finite type normalization finite
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Every integral finite-type algebra over a field or a complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local base has finite normalization, and so do its localizations. Integral schemes of finite type over these bases consequently have finite scheme normalization.
items.strategy: At every maximal ideal m of B, the preceding formal-fibre lemma implies that the completion of B_m is reduced: flatness embeds it into its generic fibre, which is geometrically regular and hence reduced. For a reduced complete equicharacteristic local ring T, its normalization in Q(T) is the product of the finite normalizations of its finitely many complete domain components, hence is finite by the complete-domain finiteness lemma. If C is the normalization of B_m, flatness embeds C⊗T into Q(T); it is integral, hence a T-submodule of that finite normalization and is finite. Faithful flatness descends its finitely many generators to C. Thus every B_m has finite normalization. J2 gives a nonzero f with B_f regular and normal. To globalize without silently assuming local finiteness is uniform: for every finite birational B⊂B′⊂Frac(B), B′_f is normal; its nonnormal locus is closed. Indeed S2 failures are detected by embedded associated primes of B′/fB′, and R1 failures by its finitely many height-one associated primes, so Serre gives a finite union of their closures. Its finite image Z_(B′) in Spec(B) is closed. For each m choose finitely many global integral elements generating the local normalization; the finite algebra they generate has m outside Z. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many such algebras; their composite has every localization normal, because at each point one selected algebra already equals the local closure. This composite is the normalization and is finite. Localization commutes with integral closure by clearing the denominators in a monic equation. The published finite-type-over-field theorem supplies the field case directly. items.title: Normalized point blowups dominate local normal surface modifications
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal two-dimensional Noetherian local domain essentially of finite type over a field or a complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local ring. Let $S$ be a normal integral modification of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $Y\to S$ be an integral modification with normal $Y$. There is a finite sequence of proper normalized point blowups $S_n\to\cdots\to S_0=S$, with centers above the finite set where $Y\to S$ fails to be an isomorphism, such that $S_n$ dominates $Y$. If $S$ is projective over $A$, so is $S_n$. For regular $S$, all these are ordinary regular point blowups.
items.strategy: All relevant normalizations are finite by the finite-type normalization helper, including after localization. The dimension/cohomology helper makes every integral modification over $A$ two-dimensional. The codimension-one helper makes $Y\to S$ an isomorphism off finitely many closed points. Its contracted curves form a finite set: each is a one-dimensional component of a fibre over that finite set. Induct on their number. If it is zero, every fibre is finite and the codimension-one helper gives an isomorphism. Otherwise choose a contracted curve $C$ over $x$. Its generic local ring is a DVR, and its residue field is the function field of the proper integral curve $C/\kappa(x)$, of transcendence degree one. Choose $u$ in this DVR with transcendental nonzero residue and write $u=a/b$ with $a,b\in\mathcal O_{S,x}$. Both have the same strictly positive valuation: valuation zero would force their residues, and hence the residue of $u$, to lie in $\kappa(x)$. Let $S'\to S$ be the normalized blowup at $x$ and let $Y'$ be the normalization of the **closure of the common generic open** in $Y\times_SS'$. Taking this dominant component avoids extraneous vertical components of the fibre product. A contracted curve of $Y'\to S'$ cannot map to a point of $Y$, for then both projections would map it to a point of their fibre product, contradicting finiteness of its normalization. It therefore maps to a contracted curve of $Y\to S$. The map $Y'\to Y$ is an isomorphism at the generic points of these curves by codimension-one isomorphism, giving an injection of the new contracted-curve set into the old one. If the chosen $C$ persists over $x'$, the invertible pullback of $\mathfrak m_x$ has a local generator $d\in\mathfrak m_{S',x'}$ and $a=da'$, $b=db'$. The same residue ratio $u=a'/b'$ now has common valuation $v_C(a')=v_C(a)-v_C(d)$, strictly smaller. Repeat at its image as long as it remains contracted. The positive integer cannot decrease indefinitely, so after finitely many steps at least this curve disappears and the finite curve count strictly decreases. Induction ends in a normal model with no contracted curves, hence an isomorphism to its dominant transform of $Y$, giving the required map to $Y$. Blowups are proper. When $S$ is projective over $A$, twist the coherent center ideal by a sufficiently high ample power to make it globally generated. Tensoring an ideal by an invertible sheaf leaves its Rees Proj unchanged, as local degree-n transition factors cancel in homogeneous fractions. The global generators therefore give one relative projective-space embedding of the blowup. Finite normalization over this projective model is projective by the explicit finite-projective helper, and composition preserves projectivity, so the whole sequence is projective over $A$. For regular $S$ a point blowup stays regular by the published arbitrary-Noetherian regular-surface point-blowup lemma, hence its normalization is the identity, and this remains true inductively.

items.title: H1 of a normal surface modification injects off its special fibre
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal two-dimensional Noetherian local domain essentially of finite type over a field or complete equicharacteristic local base, and let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective normal modification. If $U$ is the inverse image of the punctured spectrum, $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^1(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is injective.
items.strategy: Use the two-affine cover to represent a class by a Čech cocycle and glue the rank-two bundle $E$ with upper triangular transition matrix having that cocycle off the diagonal. This gives $0\to\mathcal O_X\to E\to\mathcal O_X\to0$, whose splitting is equivalent to vanishing of the class; the same construction on a refinement detects its restriction to $U$. The quotient defines a section $\sigma$ of the projective bundle $P(E)\to X$. A splitting over $U$ defines a disjoint second section $\sigma'$ there. Let $X'$ be the integral schematic closure of $\sigma'(U)$. If it missed $\sigma(X)$, $X'\to X$ would be both proper and affine, since the complement of the section is locally an affine-line chart. Proper coherent pushforward would then make its affine algebra finite. Being birational onto normal $X$, it is an isomorphism by the integral-closure argument, giving a global disjoint second section and a splitting, contrary to a nonzero class. Thus $X'$ meets $\sigma(X)$. Normalize $X'$ finitely using the normalization-finiteness helper. Its pullback $Z$ of the Cartier section is nonempty, supported in the special fibre, and effective Cartier because the integral dominant component is not contained in the section. The section's conormal bundle is $\mathcal O_X$: in a local splitting of $E$, its ideal is the coordinate of the other affine-line direction, and the kernel and quotient of the bundle extension are both $\mathcal O_X$. Pullback of this invertible Cartier ideal shows the conormal bundle of $Z$ is trivial. This contradicts the preceding positive-conormal-degree lemma on the normal modified surface. Hence every class vanishing off the special fibre is zero. The projective bundle and its normalization are projective over $A$ by twisting their coherent generators and by finite-projective composition, so all used two-affine/finite-type hypotheses hold.

items.title: Local normalized point sequences spread at closed surface points
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $X$ be a normal integral surface locally of finite type over a permitted base and $x\in X$ a closed point with two-dimensional local ring $B$. Any finite normalized point-blowup sequence over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ spreads to the same finite sequence of normalized blowups at closed points of $X$, unchanged off $x$. Its localization over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the given sequence. If $X$ is projective over a Noetherian affine base, so is the spread sequence.

Its residue field is finite over κ(x), since that fibre is finite type over κ(x). Start by blowing up x globally. Localization is flat, so its blowup localizes to the local blowup by the actual flat blowup-base-change supplier; normalization commutes with localization because the affine integral closures are computed in the common function field. The local centre of the next step is a point on the global model's fibre over x. Its finite residue field makes it a closed point of that finite-type fibre, hence of the global scheme since x is closed. Blow it up globally and normalize finitely; continue inductively. Away from x these are isomorphisms. Projectivity is preserved by twisting the centre ideal by an ample bundle and taking a finite generating family, followed by finite-over-projective normalization, exactly as in the normalized-point domination helper. The sequence is finite, so no limit or arbitrary-modification spreading theorem is used.

items.title: Normalization of a surface modification commutes with local-base completion
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal local surface domain essentially of finite type over a field or a complete equicharacteristic local base, with normal completion $\widehat A$. For an integral modification $X$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, finite normalization commutes with the base change to $\widehat A$: $(X^\nu)_{\widehat A}$ is the finite normalization of $X_{\widehat A}$. Both base-changed schemes are integral, with common function field $\operatorname{Frac}\widehat A$.
items.strategy: On an affine chart of X put B⊂K=Frac(A), and let Bν be its finite normalization in K. Flatness of Ahat over A injects B⊗A Ahat and Bν⊗A Ahat into K⊗A Ahat, the localization of the domain Ahat at the nonzero elements of A. Thus both are domains. Their fraction fields are Frac(Ahat): B contains A, lies in K and localizing B by nonzero A elements gives K, so the same after flat base change gives that common field. A→Ahat has geometrically regular formal fibres by the exact finite-type formal-fibre helper. The map Bν→Bν⊗A Ahat is its flat base change; its fibres are base-field extensions of those formal fibres (the residue extensions are finitely generated because Bν is finite type over A after clearing the given localization). They are regular by geometric regularity. Normality ascent along flat regular-fibre maps therefore makes Bν⊗A Ahat normal. It is finite and integral over B⊗A Ahat and lies in their common fraction field. Any element of that field integral over the smaller ring is also integral over this normal ring and hence belongs to it. Thus it is exactly the normalization. These identifications agree on localizations inside the common function field and glue. This proof uses the actual geometrically regular completion map and finite normalization; it does not invoke formal gluing or assume normality of an arbitrary completed ring.

items.title: Completed local degrees of finite normal surface covers
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $X\to Y$ be finite dominant of degree $n$ between integral normal surfaces in the permitted class, with $Y$ regular. At a closed $x\in X$ over a point $y\in Y$ with $\dim O_{Y,y}=2$, the complete normal local domain $\widehat{O_{X,x}}$ is finite over the complete regular local ring $\widehat{O_{Y,y}}$, and its fraction-field degree is at most $n$. In the equicharacteristic setting the latter ring is a power-series ring in two variables over its residue field.
items.strategy: Put T=O_Y,y and let C be the finite semilocal normal algebra of the cover over Spec T. It is torsion-free of generic rank n. The height-preservation theorem for integral extensions of a normal domain gives height(q)=height(m_T)=2 at each maximal ideal q of C. Thus C_q is a normal two-dimensional local ring and hence CM. A parameter pair of T generates an ideal primary for each such maximal ideal because C is finite over T, so it is a regular sequence on every C_q, and therefore on C. Thus depth_T C=2 and Auslander–Buchsbaum makes C finite free of rank n over T. Finite completion factors identify C⊗T That with the finite product of complete local rings Chat_q. Completion normality makes each nonzero factor a normal local domain; their base maps are finite local and the parameter pair remains regular, so each factor is finite free over the regular That, of some positive rank n_q. The ranks sum to n; localizing at Frac(That) turns each domain factor into its fraction field, of degree n_q≤n. Regularity and dimension two of That follow from completion-preserved regularity and unchanged embedding dimension; the equicharacteristic coefficient-field presentation gives a surjection κ(y)[[u,v]]→That. Its source and target are regular local domains of dimension two, so its prime kernel has height zero and is zero, making it an isomorphism. No global degree equality after splitting into local completion factors is assumed.

items.title: A birational morphism of regular surfaces factors through the blowup of a point where its inverse is undefined
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ and $Y$ be integral regular finite-type $k$-schemes of
pure dimension two that are proper over $k$, and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a birational morphism. Let $y\in Y$ be a
closed point at which the inverse rational map $f^{-1}\colon Y\dashrightarrow X$ is not defined
([[def-rational-map-integral-schemes]], [[def-domain-of-definition-rational-map]]). Then $f$ factors through the
blowup $b\colon \operatorname{Bl}_yY\to Y$: there is a unique $k$-morphism $g\colon X\to\operatorname{Bl}_yY$ with
$b\circ g=f$. Equivalently, the ideal $f^{-1}\mathfrak m_y\cdot\mathcal O_X$ is invertible.
items.strategy: Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and localize the proper birational map at y. The local normal-surface domination helper applies to the normalization of the dominant graph of the rational lift $X_A\dashrightarrow (\operatorname{Bl}_yY)_A$ over $X_A$. It produces a finite roof of ordinary point blowups of the regular surface $X_A$, all over its closed fibre, on which that lift is a morphism. Finite normalizations exist by the declared helper; no nonprojective Hilbert scheme is used. Choose a roof with the least number n of point blowups. If n>0, let E be the last exceptional curve and g the morphism from the final roof to the target blowup. If g(E) is a point, the universal property of a contraction descends g through the last point blowup, contradicting minimality. Otherwise g(E) is the target exceptional curve E′. Codimension-one isomorphism shows E→E′ birational. This proper nonconstant map of integral curves is quasi-finite (a positive-dimensional fibre would be the whole curve) and hence finite; a finite birational algebra over a normal affine chart of E′ equals that chart. Thus E→E′ is an isomorphism. Its induced map of conormal line bundles is generically nonzero, as g is an isomorphism at the generic points. Both are O(1) over their common constant field (identified by H0 of the isomorphic projective lines). Their Hom sheaf is O, whose global sections are that field, so this nonzero map is an isomorphism. At each point e∈E, take local equations v′ for E′ and v for E; conormal isomorphism says g*v′=uv with u a unit. The quotient local rings modulo these equations are isomorphic because E→E′ is. Consequently the maximal ideal at e is generated by the image of the target maximal ideal: modulo v this follows from the quotient isomorphism and v itself lies in that image. The local fibre ring is the finite residue field, so g is quasi-finite at e. The proper-birational quasi-finite-point helper makes g an isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of every point of E′. The whole inverse image of E′ is therefore E. Its image on X_A is the last center x, so the original fibre over y is the singleton x. The original proper birational map is then quasi-finite at x and the same helper makes it an isomorphism near y, contrary to the undefined inverse. Hence n=0 and the rational lift is a morphism on X_A. The center ideal therefore pulls back to an invertible ideal there. Globally its noninvertible locus is closed (finite presentation and local freeness of rank one are detected by a presentation and minors); any such point would lie over y because the center ideal is the unit ideal elsewhere, and would survive localization to X_A, a contradiction. Thus the ideal is invertible on X and the blowup universal property gives the factorization globally. Two lifts agree on the common generic open and everywhere by separatedness and reduced integrality. This roof/conormal argument applies to all residue fields, including finite and nonrational ones; it makes no choice of a rational point of the exceptional projective line.

items.title: Finite domination of surface modifications by a relative Hilbert scheme
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a normal Noetherian local domain of dimension two essentially of finite type over a field or a complete equicharacteristic Noetherian local ring. Let $B$ be a finite normal local $A$-domain, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a normal integral modification. There are a normal surface $X$ obtained by finitely many normalized point blowups of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, a normal integral modification $Y'\to Y$, and a finite morphism $Y'\to X$ forming a commutative diagram over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Both $X$ and $Y'$ are projective over $A$. If $A$ is regular, $X$ is regular and its normalized blowups are ordinary point blowups.
items.strategy: The normalized-point domination helper applied over $B$ first supplies a projective normal modification dominating the given $Y$. Replace $Y$ by this model; finiteness of $B/A$ and the finite/projective composition helper make it projective over $A$ with an actual global projective-space embedding. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$ and $n=[L:K]$. Its generic fibre is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}L$, which as its own closed subscheme defines a $K$-point of the published **general relative** fixed-polynomial Hilbert scheme with polynomial $n$. That Hilbert representative is proper and embeds in one projective space over $A$ for the specified embedding of $Y$; it has an actual universal finitely presented flat family. Take the schematic closure of this generic $K$-point and its finite normalization. It is a normal integral projective modification $H$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply normalized-point domination to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}A$; these give a normal projective $X$ mapping to $H$ and hence to the Hilbert scheme. Pull back the universal family to $X$. Every geometric fibre has constant Hilbert polynomial $n$, hence dimension zero by the actual Hilbert-polynomial dimension theorem, so the proper family is quasi-finite and finite. It is flat and finitely presented, hence finite locally free, of rank $n$. Its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$. On every affine open of integral $X$, its finite flat algebra is torsion-free and injects into its generic algebra $L$, so the family $Z$ is integral. Its normalization $Y'$ is finite by the normalization-finiteness helper; thus $Y'\to X$ is finite. The universal closed family gives $Z\to Y$, hence $Y'\to Y$, generically the identity of $L$. It is proper since its source is proper over $A$ and its target is separated over $A$, so is a modification. Finite-over-projective makes $Y'$ projective over $A$. Compose with the initial dominating modification to recover the original $Y$. This uses Hilbert representability only after a projective replacement, and only over a Noetherian affine base with a specified global embedding; it does not apply a finite-point or field-only Hilbert result to a nonprojective scheme. If A is regular, its normalized point blowups are ordinary regular point blowups, giving the stated regular specialization. No step requires regular A before that final specialization.

items.title: No derived residue map into structure cohomology of a normal surface modification
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For $A,X$ as in the preceding injection lemma, with residue field $\kappa$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\kappa[-1],R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X))=0$.
items.strategy: A degreewise finite free resolution $P$ of $\kappa$ gives the derived adjunction explicitly: apply sheaf/global-section Hom adjunction termwise to $P[-1]\otimes_A\mathcal O_X$ and a bounded-below injective resolution of $\mathcal O_X$. Thus the Hom group equals $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(L f^*\kappa[-1],\mathcal O_X)$. The source has cohomology at most degree one; its degree-one sheaf is $\mathcal O_{X_s}$, and its degree-zero sheaf is annihilated by the maximal ideal. Maps from the latter to the torsion-free $\mathcal O_X$ are zero, and lower cohomology gives no degree-zero maps by truncation. The truncation triangle therefore identifies the Hom group with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal O_{X_s},\mathcal O_X)$. Regard a class as an extension $0\to\mathcal O_X\to E\to\mathcal O_{X_s}\to0$. Pulling back along $\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{X_s}$ gives an extension of $\mathcal O_X$ by itself; it is split off the special fibre and hence globally split by the preceding H1 injection. Therefore $1\in\mathcal O_{X_s}$ lifts to a global section $s$ of $E$. Multiplying $s$ by the fibre ideal $I$ gives $I\to\mathcal O_X$. Since global structure functions are $A$ and global fibre-ideal functions are its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, this induces $\mathfrak m\to A$. It is multiplication by an element of the fraction field; at every height-one localization $\mathfrak m_\mathfrak p=A_\mathfrak p$, so that element belongs to $A_\mathfrak p$. Normal S2 intersection gives membership in $A$. Subtract this element from $s$. The new lift is annihilated by $I$, hence defines a splitting $\mathcal O_{X_s}\to E$ of the original extension. The Ext-one/extension correspondence here follows by an injective resolution: push out along the injection into the first injective and lift the quotient; it needs enough injectives, not enough projective module sheaves. This avoids misusing a module-only balanced-Ext assertion for sheaves.

items.title: Rational normal surface singularities and bounded modification cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. A normal two-dimensional Noetherian local domain $A$ essentially of finite type over a field or complete equicharacteristic local base defines a rational singularity if $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0$ for every normal integral proper modification $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Bounded modification H1 means these modules have uniformly bounded $A$-length. In both definitions it suffices to test projective modifications, or terminal schemes of finite normalized point-blowup sequences.
items.strategy: Normalized-point domination supplies a projective normalized point-blowup model dominating any proper normal modification. The Leray injection embeds the latter H1 into the model H1. Its finite length follows from proper coherent finiteness and isomorphism off the closed point. Conversely the restricted test schemes are themselves normal proper modifications. Thus their vanishing or a uniform bound implies the all-modifications version, and the reverse implication is immediate.

items.title: Uniform principal torsion bound for surface modification cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a normal local surface domain $A$ in the permitted finite-type class and $0\ne a\in A$, the lengths of $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)[a]$ are uniformly bounded over all normal projective modifications $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.
items.strategy: If a is a unit there is no torsion. Otherwise the preceding radical-multiple lemma gives a divisor c with A/c reduced and a|c^n. Kernels of successive multiplication by c give length(M[c^n])≤n length(M[c]); thus it suffices to bound c-torsion. Its normalization T is finite: take the finitely many reduced components of A/c and their finite normalizations, with their product in the total quotient ring. Since the punctured spectrum of the one-dimensional reduced local ring is its finitely many minimal points, T/(A/c) is a finite module supported at m and has finite length. Let Z be the Cartier divisor c=0 on X and Z′ the schematic closure of its punctured part. Z′ is reduced and has no vertical components, because it is the closure of a reduced open; each one-dimensional component dominates one of Spec(A/c)'s components. A positive-dimensional fibre over m would contain a whole one-dimensional component, impossible by dominance. Therefore Z′ is proper quasi-finite, hence finite; its algebra embeds into T. If a section s of O_Z restricts to zero on Z′, its boundary in H1(X,O) restricts to zero on the punctured preimage. The H1 injection makes that boundary zero, so s lifts from A. Its zero restriction to Z′ forces that lift to be zero in A/c because the latter embeds in the algebra of Z′; hence s=0. Thus H0(Z,O) injects into T, compatibly with A/c. The multiplication-by-c exact sequence identifies H1(X,O)[c] with H0(Z,O)/(A/c). Its length is bounded by length(T/(A/c)), uniformly in X. This gives the bound for a. The statements only use projective H1 injection, exactly as assumed; general proper modifications are handled by domination and the Leray injection when required.

items.title: Normalized point sequences and resolutions descend from completion
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For $A$ as in the preceding normalization-completion lemma, every finite sequence of normalized point blowups over $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ has a uniquely corresponding finite sequence over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with isomorphic base-changed models. Each centre lies over the closed point. If the completed terminal scheme is regular, so is the descended terminal scheme. Singular centres correspond to singular centres.
items.strategy: The starting models are normal A and Ahat. At each step, properness sends its closed centre to the closed point of the local base. The closed fibres of the corresponding models are canonically identified, so this centre corresponds to a unique closed point of the original model, with the same residue field. The matching centre ideal commutes with completion base change: on an affine chart the closed point prime contains mA, and quotienting by m identifies the fibre prime; flat base change therefore gives its extended prime exactly. Blowups commute with that flat base change by the published blowup theorem. Their finite normalizations commute by the preceding helper, establishing the model identification inductively. Their projectivity over the local affine base is preserved by blowups and finite normalization. If the completed terminal model is regular, the proper regularity-transfer helper descends regularity to the original terminal scheme. At the centres themselves the equal-completed-local-ring helper and regularity of a ring iff its completion is regular prove equivalence of regularity, hence of singularity. No algebraic descent of arbitrary modification data is claimed: only the finite point sequences and their matching fibre ideals are descended.

items.title: The number of contracted curves drops by one after factoring through a point blowup
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$, $X$, $Y$ and $f\colon X\to Y$ be as in
[[lem-birational-surface-morphism-factors-through-blowup-at-a-non-isomorphism-point]], and let $N(f)$ be the
number of integral curves of $X$ contracted by $f$, a nonnegative integer by
[[lem-fibre-components-of-a-proper-birational-morphism-of-regular-surfaces]]. Let $y\in Y$ be a closed point
such that $f$ factors through the blowup $b\colon Y'=\operatorname{Bl}_yY\to Y$, say $f=b\circ g$ with
$g\colon X\to Y'$ the factorization of the previous lemma. Then $g$ is again a birational morphism of integral
regular proper surfaces over $k$, and $N(g)=N(f)-1$.
items.strategy: The exceptional curve $E$ of $b$ is an integral curve over $\kappa(y)$ (Stacks 54.3.1, realized on this page by [[lem-blowing-up-a-regular-point-is-a-contraction]]); $g$ is proper, birational and regular by the same suppliers, and $b$ is an isomorphism over $Y\setminus\{y\}$. Exactly one component $C_0$ of $f^{-1}(y)$ dominates $E$: because $g$ is birational, its generic fibre over the generic point of $E$ is a single point, so at most one component dominates $E$, and surjectivity of $g$ forces exactly one. Every other one-dimensional component of a fibre of $f$ over $y$ lies in a fibre of $g$ over a point of $E$, and every contracted curve of $g$ is a contracted curve of $f$ different from $C_0$; conversely a curve contracted by $f$ either is $C_0$ or is contracted by $g$. Hence the two sets differ by $C_0$ alone and the count drops by one.

items.title: Grauert–Riemenschneider vanishing for the required normal surface modifications
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $R$ be regular Noetherian local of dimension two, $A$ a finite normal local $R$-domain of dimension two with $R\hookrightarrow A$ local, and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a projective normal modification, in the permitted finite-type/completion class. For its normalized dualizing module $\omega_X$ over $\omega_A=\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,R)$, $H^1(X,\omega_X)=0$.
items.strategy: The preceding geometric/cohomology helper gives no cohomology above degree one; proper coherence and the isomorphism off the closed point make $H^1(X,\omega_X)$ finite length. If nonzero, Nakayama and a residue-field functional give a nonzero map from that module to $\kappa$. Truncation yields a nonzero map $\alpha:R\Gamma(X,\omega_X[2])\to\kappa[1]$. Finite-base coherent biduality makes derived dualization with $D_A=\omega_A[2]$ faithful on bounded finite complexes. Finite-length duality takes the simple residue module to another simple module with the same annihilator, hence to $\kappa$ up to isomorphism. Projective surface duality and homothety identify the dual of $R\Gamma(X,\omega_X[2])$ with $R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The dual of $\alpha$ is therefore a nonzero map $\kappa[-1]\to R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, contradicting the preceding derived-residue-map lemma. Thus $H^1(X,\omega_X)=0$. Every duality arrow used is the actual evaluation/trace pairing over the regular subring, and no general proper duality theorem is cited in place of its proof.

items.title: Regular local surfaces have rational modification cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. A regular two-dimensional local domain in the permitted finite-type class defines a rational singularity.
items.strategy: Any proper normal modification is dominated by a normalized-point-blowup sequence. Since the base is regular these are ordinary regular point blowups. The published point-blowup pushforward theorem, including its arbitrary-Noetherian regular-center clause, makes their composite higher structure-sheaf direct images zero. Its H1 is zero because the initial base is affine. The Leray injection embeds the original modification's H1 into zero, proving rationality.

items.title: Rationality propagates to birational local surface rings
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. If a permitted normal local surface domain $A$ is rational and $A\subset B$ is a normal two-dimensional local domain with the same fraction field, essentially of finite type over $A$, then $B$ is rational. If modification H1 over $A$ is uniformly bounded, some finite normalized point-blowup sequence over $A$ has rational local rings at every closed point of its terminal surface.
items.strategy: Write B=C_q with C a finite-type A-domain in their common function field. Take its affine projective closure and finite normalization. The resulting normal projective modification X contains the same normal local ring B at a point x: normalization localizes to B, so it has exactly one point above q and leaves its local ring unchanged. The integral modification has dimension two by the dimension helper; local dimension two forces x closed (a further strict specialization would give a chain of length at least three). To test rationality of B, it suffices by normalized-point domination to test its normalized point sequences. The spreading helper extends each such sequence to X′→X. Rationality of A makes H1(X′,O)=0. The Leray exact sequence on projective X then makes R1g*O=0. Localization/Čech base change identifies its stalk at x with the tested H1 over B, so it vanishes. For bounded H1 choose a normal projective modification maximizing its integer length; such a maximum exists since the set is nonempty and bounded in N. Dominate it by a normalized point sequence. Leray injection and maximality show the terminal scheme still attains the maximum. Any further normal projective modification of this scheme has the same H1 length and hence R1g*O=0. Spread the point sequences at each closed local ring as above and use localization; they all have zero H1. The point-sequence test proves those local rings rational. No general arbitrary-modification extension or limits theorem is imported.

items.title: Powers and sections of a rational surface exceptional ideal
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a rational permitted normal local surface domain and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a normal projective modification. A coherent globally generated sheaf $F$ on $X$ has $H^1(X,F)=0$. If the scheme-theoretic closed fibre is Cartier with ideal $I=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_X$, then $H^0(X,I^n)=\mathfrak m^n$ and $H^1(X,I^n)=0$ for all $n\ge0$.
items.strategy: A coherent globally generated sheaf on the quasi-compact X admits a finite global generating family, by taking finite generators on a finite cover; hence O_X^r→F is onto. Its kernel is coherent, and H2 of that kernel is zero by the two-affine cover. Rationality gives H1(O)=0, so the long exact sequence gives H1(F)=0. Every I^n is globally generated by the finite products of generators of m, hence has zero H1. H0(I)=m: H0(O)=A and its restriction to the nonempty closed fibre has kernel m, since a unit remains a unit there and every element of m vanishes. Let x1,...,xr generate I and let K be the kernel of O^r→I. Locally one generator is a unit in a frame of I. The Koszul relations xi e_j−xj e_i therefore generate K⊗I (in frames this is the kernel of a row with a unit entry, whose Koszul relations generate); these relations are global images of ∧²O^r. Thus K⊗I is globally generated. Tensoring with the globally generated I^(n−2) shows K⊗I^(n−1) globally generated for n≥2, hence H1 zero. The sequence 0→K⊗I^(n−1)→(I^(n−1))^r→I^n→0 gives surjection on H0. Induction yields H0(I^n)=Σ xi m^(n−1)=m^n. The n=0 case is H0(O)=A and rationality.

items.title: Separable finite surface extensions preserve bounded modification cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A\subset B$ be a finite injective local extension of permitted normal local surface domains with separable fraction-field extension. If modification H1 over $A$ is uniformly bounded, so is modification H1 over $B$.
items.strategy: Let L/K have degree n, and choose b1,...,bn∈B forming a K-basis of L. The trace Gram determinant d=det(Tr(bi bj)) lies in A and is nonzero by the published separable trace pairing. For a normal projective modification Y over B, the normal-base Hilbert finite-domination helper gives a dominating normal projective Y′ finite over a normal projective modification X over A. Leray injection embeds the original H1 into H1(Y′). Normality of each target affine algebra makes field trace of every integral element regular there, so Φ:π*O_Y′→O_X^n, s↦(Tr(bi s)) is a sheaf injection. The reverse map (si)↦Σ bi si composed with Φ is its Gram matrix. Its adjugate shows d annihilates coker Φ. The long exact sequence bounds H1(Y′) modulo its d-torsion by H1(X)^n; every element in the kernel is a boundary from H0(coker Φ) and is killed by d. The uniform principal-torsion lemma over B bounds that torsion independently of Y′. The A-length of H1(X)^n is at most n times the assumed A-bound; for finite local B/A, the A-length of a finite-length B-module is [κ(B):κ(A)] times its B-length, as seen on a B-composition series. This gives a uniform B-bound on the quotient and hence on H1(Y′) and H1(Y). General normal proper modifications are handled by projective domination and Leray injection.

items.title: Surface resolution globalizes from complete local point resolutions
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $Y$ be a normal integral finite-type surface over any field. If each completed local ring at a singular closed point has a regular resolution by finitely many normalized point blowups at singular centres, then $Y$ has such a finite global sequence, proper and birational over $Y$ and an isomorphism on the regular locus.
items.strategy: The regular locus is open by the exact regular-locus helper; normality makes every codimension-one local ring regular. Its closed complement therefore has dimension zero and consists of finitely many closed points in the Noetherian surface. Each local ring there has dimension two and normal completion by normality ascent. For each such point, the preceding helper descends its given completed point-blowup resolution to a finite local sequence, preserving singularity of the centres. Spread that local sequence globally by the closed-point spreading helper. All its centres are over that original singular point and it is an isomorphism away from it. The local terminal scheme is regular; consequently the global terminal scheme is regular at every point over that original point, because localization over its local spectrum identifies those local rings. Perform these finite sequences successively at the finitely many original singular points. The sequences over later points lie in regions where all earlier operations were isomorphisms, so retain the same local input and do not alter already resolved regions. The final scheme is regular over all original singular points and over the unchanged regular locus, hence everywhere. Each step is proper by the locally H-projective/properness clause of the blowup supplier, followed by finite normalization, integral and birational; their finite composite has the asserted properties. No properness of Y over its field is assumed and no smoothness over an imperfect field is inferred.

items.title: Factorization of birational morphisms of regular surfaces into point blowups
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ and $Y$ be integral regular finite-type $k$-schemes
of pure dimension two that are proper over $k$ (for instance smooth projective surfaces over $k$). Then every
birational morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ is a composition of blowups at closed points and an isomorphism: there are
schemes $X_0=Y,X_1,\dots,X_n$ with $X_n\cong X$ over $Y$, closed points $y_{i-1}\in X_{i-1}$ with
$\mathcal O_{X_{i-1},y_{i-1}}$ regular of dimension two, and morphisms $X_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{y_{i-1}}X_{i-1}
\to X_{i-1}$ whose composition $X\to Y$ is $f$ up to the isomorphism $X\cong X_n$.

Equivalently, every proper birational morphism of such surfaces is, up to isomorphism, a composition of
contractions of exceptional curves of the first kind ([[def-exceptional-curve-and-contraction]]).
items.strategy: Induct on the finite nonnegative number N(f) of contracted curves supplied by the fibre-component lemma. The codimension-one modification lemma gives a finite set of closed points outside the largest isomorphism open. If this set is empty f is an isomorphism. Otherwise choose y in it. The rational inverse is undefined there: if it extended on an open neighbourhood, it would give a section of the proper separated f; that section is closed and contains the generic point of the integral inverse image, so is the entire reduced inverse image, making f an isomorphism there. The repaired local factorization lemma gives f=b∘g through the point blowup at y. Its source and target stay regular integral proper surfaces by point-blowup regularity and properness. The curve-count lemma gives N(g)=N(f)-1: codimension-one isomorphism gives exactly one curve dominating the exceptional curve; all other curves contracted by f remain contracted by g. Apply the induction hypothesis and compose with b. The definition of contraction identifies each point blowup as a contraction of its exceptional curve. No equality f^(-1)∘f=f or unstated rational-map contraction criterion is used.

items.title: Trace cokernels detect and bound normal surface H1
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $R$ be regular Noetherian local of dimension two and $A$ a finite normal local $R$-domain of dimension two with $R\hookrightarrow A$ local, in the permitted class. For a projective normal modification $X$, put $M=H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. There is a canonical exact sequence $0\to\Gamma(X,\omega_X)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}}\omega_A\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^2(M,R)\to0$, and the last module has the same $A$-annihilator as $M$. If one fixed nonzero $d\in A$ annihilates every such trace cokernel, then $A$ has bounded modification H1. If $A$ is rational, the trace is an isomorphism and gives an adjoint evaluation $f^*\omega_A\to\omega_X$.
items.strategy: The structure-sheaf cohomology has H0=A, H1=M of finite length and no other positive groups. Its truncation triangle is A→C→M[-1]→A[1]. Apply RHom_R(-,R), using that A is finite free over R (normal surface CM and regular parameters), and that finite-length R-duality is concentrated at Ext². The normal-surface relative duality identifies the middle dual with RΓ(X,ω_X), and GR vanishing makes that complex concentrated at degree zero. The long exact cohomology sequence is therefore exactly the displayed short exact sequence, whose injection is the trace dual to A→C. The finite-length duality helper gives equality of annihilators. If d kills all cokernels it kills M; the uniform principal-torsion bound then bounds length(M), and normalized-point domination plus Leray injection extend the bound to all proper normal modifications. If A is rational, M=0 and the trace is an isomorphism. Its inverse identifies ω_A with global sections of ω_X, whose usual sheaf evaluation produces the adjoint pullback map. All identifications are actual unit/evaluation pairings over the fixed regular base, not merely abstract module isomorphisms.

items.title: Normality and fibre cohomology of a rational surface point blowup
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a rational permitted normal local surface domain $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, its ordinary point blowup $X$ is normal. Its exceptional fibre $E$ is a projective pure CM curve, its tautological conormal line $L=\mathcal O_E(1)$ is very ample, and $H^1(E,L^n)=0$, $H^0(E,L^n)=\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ for $n\ge0$. In particular $H^0(E,O)=\kappa$ and $\deg_\kappa L=\dim_\kappa(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)-1$, which is at least one and equals one only for regular $A$.
items.strategy: Let X0 be the ordinary blowup and ν:X→X0 its finite normalization. The point ideal pulls back to invertible I′=O_X0(1), with pullback I on X; both exceptional divisors are Cartier since the schemes are integral and the centre ideal is nonzero. The preceding powers lemma gives H0(X,I^n)=m^n. There are injections m^n→H0(X0,(I′)^n)→H0(X,I^n), whose composite is the identity inclusion in the common fraction field, so both are equalities. If Q=ν*O_X/O_X0 were nonzero, then Q(n) for n≫0 would be globally generated and nonzero, so would have a nonzero global section. Serre vanishing makes H1(X0,(I′)^n)=0, and the finite projection formula makes H0 of the middle sheaf equal to H0(X,I^n)=m^n. The long exact sequence would then give H0(Q(n))=0, contradiction. Thus ν is an isomorphism and X0 is normal. Normal two-dimensional rings are CM, and their nonzerodivisor Cartier quotients are pure CM dimension one, giving E. Apply the powers lemma to 0→I^(n+1)→I^n→O_E(n)→0. H1 of both powers and H2 of the kernel vanish, giving the two fibre cohomology formulas. The blowup embedding gives very ampleness. Euler-characteristic degree is μ−1, with μ=dimκ m/m²; regularity is precisely μ=dim A=2.

items.title: Dualizing traces compose and become isomorphisms on rational modifications
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $R$ be regular local of dimension two, $A$ finite normal local over $R$, and let $g:X'\to X$ be a morphism of projective normal modifications over $A$. Their regular-base dualizing complexes are independent of the chosen projective embeddings up to the unique isomorphism preserving their duality pairings. There is a canonical trace $Rg_*D_{X'}\to D_X$, and traces compose. If every closed local ring of $X$ is rational, this trace is an isomorphism, giving $g_*\omega_{X'}=\omega_X$, $R^qg_*\omega_{X'}=0$ for $q>0$, and an adjoint evaluation $g^*\omega_X\to\omega_{X'}$. These evaluations compose along rational modifications.
items.strategy: For every bounded coherent K on X, the actual regular-base duality pairing gives Hom_X(K,D_X[j])=Hom_R(RΓ_XK,R[2+j]). Thus D_X represents that fixed functor, independently of embedding; Yoneda gives the unique pairing-preserving identification. Similarly D_X′ represents K↦Hom_X(Rg*K,D_X), since RΓ_XRg*K=RΓ_X′K, proper coherence makes Rg*K bounded coherent, and the two evaluation dualities give this equality naturally. The identity of D_X′ therefore corresponds to a trace Rg*D_X′→D_X. Applying these representing equalities successively proves composition of traces: both composites correspond to the identity of the final representing object. This construction agrees with finite closed-immersion coinduction, by its evaluation-at-one adjunction. If X has rational closed local rings, localize g at each point. At codimension-one points it is an isomorphism. At closed points the local proper modification has H0 equal to the normal local ring, H1 zero by rationality, and no higher cohomology by the two-affine projective local surface cover. Flat Čech localization therefore gives Rg*O_X′=O_X. Test the trace on F=O_X(m) and every shift. Hom_X(F,Rg*D_X′) is Hom_X′(g*F,D_X′), by the locally free pullback/direct-image adjunction, and then equals Hom_R(RΓ_X′g*F,R[2]). The finite Čech projection formula and Rg*O=O identify RΓ_X′g*F with RΓ_XF, making this precisely Hom_X(F,D_X); under evaluation it is the induced trace map. Hence trace is an isomorphism on these tests. Its bounded coherent cone is zero: for a nonzero highest cohomology sheaf of that cone, a sufficiently high positive twist has nonzero global sections and all positive cohomology zero by Serre, contradicting the tests by negative twists and shifts. Thus trace is an isomorphism. Concentration D=ω[2] gives the sheaf assertions. Its inverse followed by ordinary pullback/direct-image evaluation defines g*ω_X→ω_X′. Counits compose and their trace identifications are the ones just proved, so these maps compose. This supplies the exact rational-case relative trace needed for canonical principalization without importing an unspecified proper f-shriek theorem.

items.title: Canonical adjunction for a Cartier fibre curve
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a normal projective surface modification $X$ over a finite normal local domain $A$ of a regular two-dimensional local ring $R$, let $E$ be a Cartier closed fibre with residue field $\kappa$ and conormal $L=O_X(-E)|_E$. Then $\omega_E=\omega_X|_E\otimes L^{-1}$ is a projective-curve canonical module, up to the harmless one-dimensional residue-field normalization. At a regular point of $X$ the surface canonical module is invertible.
items.strategy: The ideal sequence 0→O_X(-E)→O_X→O_E→0 is a length-one locally free resolution. Applying internal Hom(-,ω_X[2]) gives i!D_X=(ω_X(E)|E)[1], because multiplication by the Cartier equation is injective on the CM torsion-free ω_X. Closed-immersion coinduction identifies its duality pairing over R with that inherited from X. On κ, the regular-parameter Koszul resolution and finite-length duality give RHom_R(κ,R[2]) a simple one-dimensional κ-module in degree zero. Choose one nonzero identification of that line with κ; finite-ring coinduction then identifies the inherited pairing with the usual curve pairing over κ. By its representing property this is the curve canonical module. A different line identification rescales it by a unit and changes none of the assertions. The conormal is L, so O_X(E)|E=L^-1 and the formula follows. For the last assertion work at a closed point of an embedding in projective space over R. Its ambient local ring T is regular and its quotient B=O_X,x is regular. Lift a minimal basis of the kernel of m_T/m_T²→m_B/m_B² to c=dim T−dim B elements of the defining ideal. They extend to regular parameters of T. The quotient by them is a regular local domain of dimension dim B and surjects onto B; its remaining prime kernel has height zero and hence is zero. Thus the defining ideal is that regular sequence. Its Koszul dual Ext is free of rank one over B, so the concentrated canonical module is invertible. Localization proves the assertion at every regular point.

items.title: Canonical modules transform by the exceptional divisor at a regular point blowup
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For the point blowup $b:X'\to X$ of a regular Noetherian surface in the fixed regular-base dualizing setting, with exceptional divisor $E$, there is a canonical generic-compatible identification $\omega_{X'}=b^*\omega_X\otimes O_{X'}(E)$.
items.strategy: The assertion is local at the centre. Let T=O_X,x be its two-dimensional regular local ring, choose its parameter pair u,v, and trivialize ω_X locally. The published incidence presentation realizes the blowup as the Cartier hypersurface uV−vU=0 in P1_T. Relative Laurent duality on P1_T gives its canonical complex O(-2)[1] relative to the base dualizing module T[2]. Cartier coinduction from the hypersurface's O(-1)→O resolution multiplies the canonical line by O(1) and subtracts one shift; the resulting surface module is O(-1) times the pulled-back base line. The tautological O(1) on the blowup is O(-E), so O(-1)=O(E). Coinduction and Laurent evaluation preserve the generic identification. Outside the centre b is an isomorphism. These identifications glue: on overlaps they induce the same identification of duality pairings, and the representing-property uniqueness of the regular-base dualizing helper forces equality. This is a local Koszul/Laurent computation; it does not assert an unproved formula for a blowup at a singular point.

items.title: Canonical pullback is surjective after blowing up a rational singular point
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a nonregular rational normal local surface domain in the permitted regular-base dualizing setting, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its ordinary point blowup, $E$ its exceptional divisor and $I=O_X(1)$. Then $H^1(X,\omega_X\otimes I^n)=0$ for $n\ge0$ and the canonical evaluation $f^*\omega_A\to\omega_X$ is surjective. The assertion localizes to closed rational singular points on a projective normal modification of the same regular base.
items.strategy: The rational blowup helper gives normal X and a CM projective curve E with H0(O_E)=κ, very ample L=I|E, and degree at least two because A is nonregular. Cartier adjunction gives ω_X|E=ω_E⊗L. For n≥0 the curve twist ω_E⊗L^(n+1) has zero H1: the globally generated positive-degree L^(n+1) is nontrivial (its degree is positive by tensor additivity). Tensor the Cartier ideal sequence to obtain 0→ω_X(n+1)→ω_X(n)→ω_E⊗L^(n+1)→0. The curve vanishing makes H1(ω_X(n+1))→H1(ω_X(n)) onto. Serre vanishing starts at large n and downward induction proves all stated vanishings. In particular H0(ω_X) surjects onto H0(E,ω_X|E). The degree-at-least-two curve helper makes the latter restriction globally generated. Hence the cokernel of global evaluation vanishes on E by Nakayama; its support is proper over the local base and misses the closed fibre, so is empty. Rational trace identifies H0(ω_X)=ω_A, proving the canonical evaluation surjective. For the localization assertion use the global rational trace compatibility helper: over a rational local point Rg*O=O, and its compatible trace identifies the localized pushforward of the global canonical module with the local canonical module. The Cartier-curve pairing and its one-dimensional residue normalization are unchanged; the same local proper argument therefore applies. No finite-over-R hypothesis is imposed falsely on a local ring of an intervening modification.

items.title: Top differential lattices map into point-blowup canonical modules
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a regular local surface of characteristic $p$, and let $A_0\subset A$ have coherent differential module $\Omega_{A/A_0}$ free of finite rank $r$. Choose $\omega_A=\wedge^r\Omega_{A/A_0}$. Every finite sequence of regular point blowups $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ has a generic-compatible map $(\wedge^r\Omega_{X/A_0})^{**}\to\omega_X$.
items.strategy: Induct through one point blowup b:X′→X. Let F=Ω_X/A0 modulo torsion and let V=F**; the preceding regular-surface helper makes V a vector bundle of rank r, and D_X=(∧^rΩ_X/A0)**=det V. On a standard point-blowup chart T[t]/(ut−v), the relative differential presentation is generated by dt with relation u dt=0 (and v dt=t u dt). Hence Ω_X′/X is the exceptional curve differential line, locally O_E dt; its stalk at the generic point of E has length one over the exceptional DVR. At that DVR, Ω_X′/A0 modulo torsion is a free lattice F′ of rank r. The image J of b*F in it has full rank and quotient of length at most one, since it is a quotient of Ω_X′/X. Under the generic identification, J is also the image lattice of b*F in b*V, and is contained in that free lattice; its index there has length d≥0. Determinants over the DVR give det F′=det(b*V) multiplied by a scalar of valuation d−length(F′/J)≥−1. Thus the top differential line on X′ is contained in b*D_X(E) along E, and equals b*D_X away from E, where b is an isomorphism. The codimension-one reflexive-extension criterion makes this a global generic-compatible inclusion D_X′→b*D_X(E). Compose it with the inductive map b*D_X(E)→b*ω_X(E) and the regular-point canonical transform identification to obtain D_X′→ω_X′. The initial map is the chosen equality on Spec A. This explicit lattice bound accommodates torsion and failure of local freeness in Ω_X; it does not assume the source's terse either/or determinant formula without proving the needed bound.

items.title: Rational normal surfaces reduce to an invertible canonical module
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. A rational normal local surface domain in the permitted regular-base dualizing setting admits a finite sequence of ordinary point blowups at singular closed points, with each model normal and projective, whose terminal canonical module is invertible. Its closed local rings remain rational; an invertible canonical module with finite injective dimension makes them Gorenstein.
items.strategy: The canonical module ω_A is finite torsion-free generic rank one. Principalize it by the fractional-ideal blowup helper and dominate the finite normalization of that blowup by normalized point blowups. Rationality propagates to the local rings of every normal model, and the rational point-blowup normality helper shows every normalization step is the identity, so the sequence consists of ordinary blowups. At a singular terminal point x, each ancestor is singular: a point blowup of a regular surface stays regular, and an isomorphism does too. At each ancestor the map to the next model is either an isomorphism locally or the blowup of that rational singular point. The canonical surjectivity helper, together with composition of the rational canonical evaluations, therefore gives a surjection from the terminal pullback of ω_A onto ω_terminal at x. Its torsion-free rank-one quotient on the principalizing model is invertible; the dominating model has the same invertible quotient L. Since ω_terminal is torsion-free, the surjection factors through L_x. A surjection of this invertible module onto a torsion-free rank-one module is an isomorphism: trivialize L_x, whose surjection has generically zero kernel and hence zero kernel in the local domain. At regular terminal points the canonical module is invertible by the regular-point part of Cartier adjunction. Thus it is invertible everywhere. To retain only singular centres, delete any regular-centre step and all later centres over it: its entire descendant region is regular by regular point-blowup preservation. The retained centres lie in the unchanged open complement, where their point blowups agree with the original sequence; glue them to the identity on the deleted region. This is precisely the global point blowup at each retained closed centre, since its ideal is the unit ideal on that region. Canonical invertibility still holds on the unchanged singular region and on the regular deleted region. The finite final sequence therefore has only singular centres. Rationality of its closed local rings follows from propagation. Finally an invertible canonical module identifies, after local trivialization, the local dualizing complex with the local ring shifted by two; its finite injective dimension means the local ring has finite injective dimension, the Gorenstein condition. No rational-double-point resolution or quadratic-chart termination is asserted by this reduction.

items.title: Degree-p inseparable extensions of complete regular surfaces have bounded H1
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A=k[[u,v]]$ have characteristic $p>0$, let $L/K$ be a purely inseparable degree-$p$ extension of its fraction field, and let $B$ be the finite normalization of $A$ in $L$. Then normal modification H1 over $B$ is uniformly bounded.
items.strategy: Write L=K[z]/(z^p-f), clearing denominators by pth powers so f∈A, and let z∈B. The p-basis subfield helper chooses a finite-index k′⊂k such that df is nonzero relative to A0=k′[[u^p,v^p]]. The explicit p-monomial basis identifies Ω_A/A0 as finite free of rank r=[p-basis rank of k/k′]+2: A is the quotient of A0 by adjoining finitely many exponent-p coefficient generators and u,v, whose defining pth-power equations have zero differentials. Choose η of degree r−1 with θ=η∧df nonzero in ω_A=∧^rΩ_A/A0. The normal-surface degree-p trace and finite coinduction give c:∧^rΩ_B/A0→ω_B=Hom_A(B,ω_A), α↦(b↦Tr(bα)). For i=0,...,p−1 take α_i=η∧z^(p−1−i) dz. Its functional on z^j is δ_ij θ: reduce powers using z^p=f and apply the coefficient-p−1 formula. Hence c has full generic image in the rank-one B-module ω_B. Its coherent cokernel is therefore killed by some fixed nonzero d∈B (clear denominators for finitely many generators). For every normal projective modification Y over B, the regular specialization of Hilbert finite domination gives a dominating normal projective Y′ finite over a regular point-blowup modification X over A. Apply the extended differential trace to Y′→X, then the differential-lattice canonical comparison on X. Finite coinduction and the pairing-preserving dualizing identification give a map ∧^rΩ_Y′/A0→ω_Y′ that generically equals c. Forms from B pull back to global forms on Y′, so the image of Γ(Y′,ω_Y′)→ω_B contains c(∧^rΩ_B/A0): both maps agree generically and ω_B is torsion-free. The trace here is precisely the finite coinduction counit followed by the regular-base trace, whose compatibility follows from the representing-property construction. Thus its cokernel is killed by the fixed d. The trace-cokernel/finite-length duality helper bounds H1(Y′), and Leray injection bounds H1(Y). This proves uniform boundedness without substituting the zero ordinary field trace for the differential trace.
