items.title: The tangent conic of a rational Gorenstein surface singularity
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a nonregular rational normal local surface domain in the permitted canonical-module setting, with $\omega_A\cong A$. Then its point blowup is normal with trivial canonical module. Its exceptional conormal $L$ has degree two and $\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}=2n+1$. For a minimal generating triple of $\mathfrak m$, the associated graded ring is $\kappa[T_1,T_2,T_3]/(q)$ for one nonzero quadratic $q$, so the exceptional fibre is its plane conic.
items.strategy: The canonical evaluation is a surjection from O_X to the torsion-free rank-one ω_X, so is an isomorphism; its kernel is generically zero and hence zero. The point-blowup helper gives H0(E,O)=κ, H1(E,O)=0 and H1(E,L^n)=0 for n≥0. Cartier adjunction gives ω_E=L^-1. Since L is globally generated and nontrivial, H0(L^-1)=0 by the product-of-sections argument, while Serre duality gives H1(L^-1)=H0(O)∨ of dimension one. Thus χ(L^-1)=-1 and χ(O)=1, giving deg L^-1=-2 and hence deg L=2 by inverse-degree additivity. Tensor-power additivity yields χ(L^n)=1+2n, and the fibre cohomology formula gives the stated Hilbert function. At n=1 it gives a minimal generating triple. The polynomial ring on their initial classes surjects onto gr_m A; at degree two its six-dimensional space maps onto a five-dimensional space, giving one nonzero q. Multiplication by that nonzero quadratic in the polynomial domain is injective, so the degree-n part of its quotient has dimension binom(n+2,2)−binom(n,2)=2n+1. The surjection from this quotient to gr_m A is therefore an isomorphism in every degree. Taking Proj identifies the exceptional fibre with the conic. This avoids applying a smooth-curve Riemann–Roch theorem to a nonreduced exceptional curve.

items.title: Nonsquare tangent-conic surface singularities terminate under point blowups
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a nonregular rational normal local surface domain in the permitted class with invertible canonical module and normal completion, if its tangent-conic quadratic is not a scalar times a square, repeatedly blowing up its singular points terminates in a regular model. Each blowup has at most one singular successor; that successor is residue-field rational and again has nonsquare tangent conic.
items.strategy: Choose generators x1,x2,x3 and lift the unique quadratic relation to Σ aij xi xj=Σ aijk xi xj xk. On the x1-chart put yi=xi/x1; dividing the relation gives the exceptional conic q(1,y2,y3). At a singular closed point p the fibre equation belongs to the square of its plane maximal ideal: otherwise quotienting by it lowers the two-dimensional plane cotangent space by one, so the surface local maximal ideal generated by x1 and two lifts would have embedding dimension at most two and be regular. If its residue degree exceeded one, the quadratic square-ideal lemma would force q to be a scalar square. Thus p is κ-rational. Change the triple to put p=(1,0,0); q then involves only T2,T3 and is a nonsquare binary quadratic. If it has a κ-root it splits into two distinct κ-lines, with unique singular point their intersection; otherwise the conic has only the rational vertex. Hence there is only one possible singular point. Absorb coefficients a11,a12,a13 with zero residues into the cubic part. Singularity of the chart further forces the constant cubic coefficient a111 to lie in m (else the chart relation eliminates x1 as a cotangent generator). Write it modulo (x2,x3) as b x1. The quadratic relation in the successor generators x1,y2,y3 then restricts on the plane x1=0 to precisely the same nonsquare binary quadratic in y2,y3; the other terms have an x1 factor. Its successor is therefore again case I, and its rational singular point cannot lie on x1=0. Thus the original fixed x1 cuts out the exceptional divisor at every point in a hypothetical infinite successor chain. The residue fields all remain κ. The fixed-coordinate helper constructs a nonsingular arc from the completion onto a complete DVR. Completion normality gives regularity at its height-one kernel; the formal-arc termination helper makes the completed local blowup chain regular after finitely many steps. Blowup flat base change and the equal closed-fibre local completions helper identify its completions with those of the original chain, so completion-preserved regularity gives the same regularity on the original chain, contradiction. There is only one branch, so the finite chain resolves all singular points in this case. No square-conic case is asserted.

items.title: A square-conic blowup has cubic-controlled singular successors
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a rational Gorenstein normal local surface singularity with square tangent conic, choose $\mathfrak m=(x_1,x_2,z)$ and a relation $z^2=\sum a_{ijk}x_ix_jx_k$. There is a nonzero homogeneous cubic $H\in\kappa[X_1,X_2]$ whose zero scheme on the reduced exceptional line contains all singular successors. Simple closed zeros have nonsquare successor conic and therefore finite resolution. There is at most one possible square-conic successor, and it is $\kappa$-rational. This is a branching statement, not termination of the continuing square branch.
items.strategy: The exceptional fibre is twice a line C=P1_κ by the tangent-conic helper. On the x1-chart write y=x2/x1,w=z/x1. The relation is w²=x1(Σ aijk yi yj yk), and the restriction of the bracket to C is h(y)=ā111+ā112 y+ā122 y²+ā222 y³. At its generic DVR, the ideal of C is (x1,w). The Cartier exceptional divisor has multiplicity two, so v(x1)=2; since (x1,w) is the DVR maximal ideal, v(w)=1. The displayed relation forces its bracket to be a unit, so h is not identically zero. The x2-chart gives the corresponding homogeneous cubic H on C. At a closed point of C its local maximal ideal is generated by x1,w and a lift g of the prime polynomial on the affine line. If H is nonzero there, the relation expresses x1 modulo the square of that maximal ideal, leaving at most two cotangent generators; the normal local surface ring is then regular. Thus every singular successor is a zero of H. If its prime polynomial divides H just once, its tangent quadratic has the form w²−x1(αx1+βw+u g), with u nonzero in the residue field. It is not a scalar square: the missing g² coefficient would force the g coefficient of a proposed linear square to be zero, contradicting the nonzero x1g coefficient. The nonsquare-conic helper resolves such a branch, even when its residue field extends κ. A remaining square successor must be a multiple closed zero of H. A degree-three homogeneous polynomial on P1 has total zero-degree three, so it has at most one multiple closed zero, whose degree must be one. This proves finite branching and the rationality of the unique possible continuing square branch. Higher-order terms and coordinate square corrections still need analysis to prove that branch terminates; they are not discarded here.

items.title: The double-plus-simple cubic surface branch terminates
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a rational Gorenstein normal local surface in the permitted canonical-module setting, with normal completion and generators $\mathfrak m=(x,y,z)$. If $z^2+a xy^2\in z\mathfrak m^2+(x,y)^4$ for a unit $a$, all its singular point-blowup branches terminate. A continuing square branch has unchanged residue field and the same $x$ defining every successive exceptional divisor.
items.strategy: Ordinary rational point blowups are normal; rationality propagates to closed local rings, and canonical pullback from a local trivialization is a surjection onto a torsion-free rank-one module, hence an isomorphism. Thus the rational Gorenstein and normal-completion hypotheses persist. Write an exact relation z²+a xy²+b x²z+c xyz+d y²z+e x⁴+f x³y+g x²y²+h xy³+i y⁴=0, after absorbing z²m into a unit coefficient and dividing by it. The reduced controlling cubic is āXY²: its simple X=0 root has a nonsquare successor; its only possible continuing square successor is the rational point u=y/x=v=z/x=0. Divide by x² in that chart to obtain v²+a xu²+b xv+c xuv+d xu²v+e x²+f x²u+g x²u²+h x²u³+i x²u⁴=0. Its quadratic is V²+b̄XV+ēX². If nonsquare, the existing case-I lemma terminates. If square choose a residue lift δ with b̄=2δ̄ and ē=δ̄², and put w=v+δx. Then b′=b−2δ and e′=e−bδ+δ² belong to the old m, hence b′=xB,e′=xE on this chart. The full new equation is w²+a xu²+c xuw+d xu²w+x²[Bw+(f−cδ)u+(g−dδ)u²+h u³+i u⁴]+x³E=0. Its cubic modulo w is X(āU²+ρXU+σX²), with ā≠0. X=0 is simple, so any multiple closed root is unique, rational, and lies at (X:U)=(1:ε). It satisfies āε²+ρε+σ=0 and 2āε+ρ=0, characterizing a double polynomial root in every characteristic without dividing by 2. Replace u by u−εx, using a local residue lift. The same x remains unchanged; the cubic becomes āXu², while all other cubic terms are divisible by w and all degree-at-least-four terms belong to w(m′)²+(x,u)⁴. Thus the broad invariant is preserved, with unit coefficient. Every continuing square step uses the x-chart, has the same residue field and has centre ideal generated by the same x; both shifts preserve that ideal. An infinite such branch would give the nonsingular formal arc and surjective completion map supplied by the direct-union helper. Normal completion makes its height-one kernel regular, so the formal-arc generator/exponent termination lemma contradicts an infinite singular branch; closed-fibre completion comparison transfers this regularity to the original sequence. Simple-root side branches terminate by case I. The exact coefficient expansions, root conditions and chart normalization are retained in square-conic-closure.md, §1; no quartic term or coordinate correction is suppressed.

items.title: A triple-cubic surface branch reduces after two successors
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. For a rational Gorenstein normal local surface in the permitted setting with square tangent conic, if its nonzero controlling cubic is a scalar times a cube, its continuing branch enters the nonsquare case or the double-plus-simple cubic class after at most two successive square successors. This allows every characteristic and residue field.
items.strategy: Ordinary rational point blowups are normal; rationality propagates to closed local rings, and canonical pullback from a local trivialization is a surjection onto a torsion-free rank-one module, hence an isomorphism. Thus the rational Gorenstein and normal-completion hypotheses persist. Choose generators so the cubic is āY³ with ā≠0. Group the relation as z²+a y³+β x²z+γ x⁴∈J1=(x³y,x²y²,xyz,y²z), a unit, absorbing z²m into a unit coefficient. The sole possible singular x-chart successor has quadratic P(X,V)=V²+β̄XV+γ̄X²; if nonsquare it is case I. If square, choose δ lifting β̄=2δ̄,γ̄=δ̄² and make the old-ring correction w=z+δx². This preserves J1 because xyz changes by x³y and y²z by x²y². The new x²w and x⁴ coefficients belong to m. Expanding them in (x,y,w), absorbing a w² coefficient into a unit, and grouping terms gives z²+a y³+ρx³y+σx⁵∈J2=(x³z,x²y²,xyz,y²z). Write its right side Ax³z+Bx²y²+Cxyz+Dy²z. Its exact x-chart relation is v²+a xu³+ρx²u+σx³−Ax²v−Bx²u²−Cxuv−Dxu²v=0. The origin is singular: otherwise x is in the maximal-ideal square (the quotient by x has the double-line cotangent generators u,v), and this equation puts the square of a regular parameter v in the third power, impossible. Its quadratic is v², and its controlling cubic is X²(ρ̄U+σ̄X). Normality of its next rational blowup forces this cubic nonzero by the generic exceptional-DVR argument, so ρ or σ is a unit. If ρ is a unit its cubic is double-plus-simple, and an invertible linear choice of simple coordinate ρu+σx and double coordinate x puts it in the preceding lemma. If ρ is a nonunit, σ is a unit and ρ=xr on the chart. Swap X=u,Y=x,Z=v. The full relation becomes Z²+(σ+rX)Y³+aX³Y−AY²Z−BX²Y²−CXYZ−DX²YZ=0. Its last four terms lie in (X³Z,X²Y²,XYZ,Y²Z); hence it is already the corrected relation with new ρ=a a unit and new σ=0. One more blowup reaches the double-plus-simple class. In particular, relabel the original E8-form generators x=y_old, y=x_old, z=z_old to obtain T′ with a=1,ρ=0,σ=1. Its actual successor v²+y_old u³+y_old³ is the T1 σ-unit chart. The T2 swap X=u,Y=y_old gives v²+Y³+X³Y, which is T′ with new ρ=1,σ=0. Its next X-chart is w²+X s³+X²s, whose cubic X²s enters the stable class. The proof uses neither division by 2 or 3 nor a geometric-factorization assumption. The complete old-ring square correction and T1/T2 equations are in square-conic-closure.md, §2.

items.title: Rational Gorenstein normal surface singularities resolve by point blowups
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. A rational Gorenstein normal local surface domain in the permitted canonical-module setting with normal completion is resolved by finitely many ordinary blowups at singular closed points. Every model is normal, its closed local rings are rational, and its canonical module is invertible; the terminal model is regular and projective over the local base. It is unchanged off the original closed point.
items.strategy: Rationality makes each ordinary point blowup normal and propagates to its local rings. At a rational singular point, trivialize the local invertible canonical module; canonical pullback is a surjection from O onto a torsion-free generic-rank-one module, hence an isomorphism, so all singular successors remain Gorenstein. Their completions are normal by the permitted finite-type normal-completion helper. Nonregular points have the plane-conic tangent ring from the Hilbert-function lemma. If its quadratic is nonsquare, case I terminates. If square, its nonzero controlling cubic has singular successors only at its finitely many closed roots. Simple closed roots give nonsquare successors. A multiple closed root of a cubic has degree one and is unique; its factorization is either double-plus-simple or a cube, handled by the two preceding full chart lemmas. The triple case enters a stable or nonsquare branch after at most two continuing square successors, and the stable branch terminates by the same-exceptional-parameter arc argument. Thus no infinite singular-successor branch exists. The tree is finitely branching (at most three closed cubic zeros at a square point and at most one successor in case I). If it were infinite, repeatedly choosing a child with infinitely many descendants would give an infinite path, using the declared AC/DC. Hence it is finite. Blow up those finitely many singular points in their ancestor order. Locality and the preceding preservation statements give a regular terminal surface, normality at every step, projectivity and the isomorphism off the original closed point. No ADE classification diagrams or unproved square-persistence assertion are imported.

items.title: A complete normal surface resolution converts to normalized point blowups
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. If a complete equicharacteristic normal local surface domain $A$ admits a proper birational regular model, then it admits a regular terminal model obtained by finitely many normalized point blowups. The centres can all be chosen singular; the normalizations are finite.
items.strategy: Choose the finite regular power-series subring R of A. Let Z→Spec A be a regular proper birational model, and choose a normalized-point sequence W over A dominating Z. W is projective over A and R, with finite normalizations, by the exact domination helper. Its finite singular set follows from the open regular locus and normality in codimension one. W→Z is proper since W is proper over A and Z separated; a closed singular w therefore maps to a closed z. The modification dimension helper gives both local rings dimension two. O_Z,z is regular and rational, and rationality propagation makes O_W,w rational in their common fraction field. W has the regular-base projective canonical module; the local canonical principalization helper reduces these finitely many rational points to invertible canonical modules by ordinary singular-point blowups. Their normal completions follow from the exact permitted formal-fibre helper. The rational-Gorenstein resolution theorem then resolves them by further ordinary singular-point blowups. Spread all finite local sequences at those closed points to W. The terminal scheme is regular over each original singular point and on the unchanged regular open, so globally regular. Composing its ordinary blowups with the initial normalized-point sequence gives the required normalized-point sequence over A. If an initial centre was regular, its entire descendant region remains regular by regular point-blowup preservation. Delete that regular-centre step and all later centres over it; retained centres lie in its unchanged open complement and their point blowups glue with the identity on the deleted regular region. Repeat for the finitely many such subtrees. The final regular model still exists, with only singular centres. No general alteration equivalence, mixed-characteristic theorem or formal-gluing theorem is used.

items.title: Complete equicharacteristic normal surfaces resolve by normalized point blowups
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Every complete equicharacteristic Noetherian normal local domain $A$ of dimension two admits a regular resolution by finitely many normalized point blowups at singular closed points. All normalizations are finite and the resulting morphism is projective, birational, and an isomorphism off the original closed point.
items.strategy: Choose a finite injective regular complete power-series subring R and argue strongly by the finite fraction-field degree D, for every such finite pair R⊂A. Degree one gives A=R because R is normal. If a proper intermediate field L exists, its normalization B over R is finite and normal in L; since it is a domain finite over complete local R, the finite-completion-factor decomposition has just one factor, making B local and complete. Its degree is smaller than D, so induction gives a regular projective normalized-point model Y over B. Normalize the dominant component of Y×_B Spec A. It is finite over Y (the fibre product is finite and its normalization is finite in the permitted class), projective over R and A, normal, and birational over A with finite cover degree [Frac A:L]. Its finite singular set consists of closed points. At each singular x over y, y is closed because the cover is finite; the local ring of the regular modification Y has dimension two. The completed-local degree-bound helper makes A_x^hat finite over a regular completed local power-series ring with degree at most [Frac A:L]<D. Apply the strong induction hypothesis there. Completion descent gives a local normalized-point resolution, and closed-point spreading integrates the finitely many sequences to obtain a regular proper birational model over A. The conversion helper gives a regular normalized-point sequence over A. If no proper intermediate field exists, the extension is separable or purely inseparable of degree p: choose a nonseparable element; its separable p-power would give an intermediate field unless in the base, and a purely inseparable degree larger than p would also have one. In the separable case the separable transfer helper gives bounded H1 from regular rational R; in the degree-p case the differential-trace helper does so. Maximal-H1 reduction gives a normalized-point model with rational closed local rings. Canonical principalization reduces its finite singular set to invertible canonical modules, and the now proved rational-Gorenstein resolution theorem resolves the remaining points. Spreading those finite ordinary blowup sequences gives a regular normalized-point model over A. Every used model has finite normalization, open regular locus and normal local completion by the already closed permitted-base endpoints; no general excellence theorem is substituted for them. Finally delete regular-centre subtrees as in the conversion lemma, preserving a regular terminal model and leaving only singular centres. The induction is well founded because every completed local cover in the intermediate case has strictly smaller degree. All models stay projective by finite-normalization projectivity.

items.title: Resolution of normal surface singularities
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice, inherited from the completion and commutative-algebra suppliers. Let $k$ be a field of arbitrary characteristic and let $Y$ be a normal integral scheme (every local ring is an integrally closed domain) of finite type over $k$ of dimension two. There is a finite sequence $Y_n\to\cdots\to Y_1\to Y_0=Y$ such that each $Y_i\to Y_{i-1}$ is the blowup at a closed point lying above a singular point of $Y$ followed by finite normalization, each $Y_i$ is normal and proper over $Y$, and $Y_n$ is regular. Consequently the composite $\pi:Y_n\to Y$ is a proper birational morphism, is an isomorphism over the regular locus of $Y$, and resolves all singularities of $Y$. Regularity is the conclusion over an arbitrary field; smoothness over $k$ follows if $k$ is perfect. No properness of $Y$ over $k$ is required.
items.strategy: For every singular closed point y of the normal finite-type field surface Y, its local ring has dimension two and normal equicharacteristic completion by the exact regular-locus and formal-fibre helpers. The complete-normal-surface resolution theorem gives a finite normalized point-blowup resolution of that completion; its proof uses the finite regular power-series degree induction, the separable and degree-p trace bounds, rational canonical principalization, and the corrected Lipman triple-cubic/stable-cubic termination proved in the new branch lemmas. Normalization commutes with completion because the completion map has geometrically regular fibres: the finite normal chart algebra stays normal, embeds in Frac of the completed base and is finite birational over the base-changed unnormalized chart. Thus matching closed-fibre points and flat blowup base change descend the finite normalized sequence to the original local ring. Its terminal regularity descends by proper completion transfer. The normal surface has open regular locus and is regular in codimension one, so its singular set is a finite set of closed points. The local-to-global helper spreads the finite local sequences successively at those points, leaving each other region unchanged; the final finite global normalized-point sequence is regular everywhere, proper and birational over Y, and an isomorphism on its original regular locus. Its normalizations are finite by the permitted finite-type normalization helper, and Y0=Y because the original surface is normal. No properness over the field is used. Over a perfect field regular finite-type schemes are smooth by the actual published supplier; over an imperfect field the claimed conclusion is regularity. All characteristic cases are covered: square/root corrections use polynomial square and repeated-root identities without dividing by 2 or 3; triple-cubic normality forces a unit alternative and reduces the E8 successor to the stable fixed-coordinate arc case. The durable exact chart proof is square-conic-closure.md. No arbitrary-Noetherian alteration equivalence, unproved ADE classification or cap obstruction enters.

items.title: What this page does and does not prove about contractions and resolution
items.statement:
The page's commissioned claims comprise the intrinsic exceptional-curve and contraction definition, universal property and uniqueness of a contraction, the point-blowup direction, negativity of contracted curves, factorization of proper birational morphisms of regular surfaces, and resolution of normal integral finite-type surfaces over every field and characteristic ([[def-exceptional-curve-and-contraction]], [[lem-universal-property-of-a-contraction]], [[lem-blowing-up-a-regular-point-is-a-contraction]], [[thm-negativity-for-exceptional-curves-on-smooth-surfaces]], [[thm-factorization-of-birational-morphisms-of-smooth-surfaces]], [[thm-resolution-of-normal-surface-singularities]]). The surface resolution concludes regularity over an arbitrary field and smoothness only over a perfect field.

The page does not claim Castelnuovo's existence criterion for contracting every exceptional curve on a proper regular surface, negative definiteness of the complete intersection matrix of a reducible exceptional divisor, the arbitrary-Noetherian alteration/resolution equivalence of Stacks 54.14.5, or a resolution theorem in dimension at least three. These are outside the commissioned scope. The corrected local proof of the commissioned surface theorem includes the triple-cubic and stable-cubic square-conic cases, without adding these stronger statements.

items.title: Normalization of a non-normal surface is not a point blowup
items.statement:
**False claim refuted:** a normalization of a singular surface is a finite composition of point blowups, or more generally a proper modification that is an isomorphism outside a finite set of points.

Let $k$ be any field of characteristic $\neq2$ and let
$$S=\operatorname{Spec}k[x,y,z]/(x^2-y^2z)\subseteq\mathbb A^3_k.$$
Write $A=k[x,y,z]/(x^2-y^2z)$ and $B=k[u,y]$, and let
$$\nu\colon\operatorname{Spec}B=\mathbb A^2_k\longrightarrow S,\qquad x\mapsto yu,\quad y\mapsto y,\quad z\mapsto u^2.$$
Then:

1. $S$ is an integral surface, its Jacobian singular locus is the whole $z$-axis $x=y=0$, and $S$ is not normal.
2. The map $\nu$ is the finite birational normalization of $S$ and is an isomorphism exactly over $\{y\neq0\}$. Over every geometric point of the $z$-axis with $z\neq0$, its fibre has two distinct points.
3. Consequently $\nu$ is not a point blowup, not a finite composition of point blowups of $S$, and not any proper modification of $S$ that is an isomorphism over the complement of a finite set of points: every point blowup is an isomorphism off its centre, whereas $\nu$ fails to be an isomorphism over infinitely many points of the $z$-axis.

The target is nonnormal, so this example records the failure of point-blowup factorization when the target regularity hypothesis is dropped. Normalization is a different operation from point blowups.
items.strategy: Show A=k[y,yu,u²] is a domain and B=k[u,y] is the full integral closure by finiteness, a shared fraction field, and integral closedness. Exhibit nonnormality at the origin via the integral element u=x/y, two geometric points over the nonzero z-axis, and the finite-center obstruction for point blowups.

items.title: Blowing up a smooth point: charts, exceptional curve, and contraction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be an integral regular finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension two, and let
$p\in S$ be a $k$-rational closed point. Let $\pi\colon S'=\operatorname{Bl}_pS\to S$ be the blowup of $p$,
with exceptional curve $E=\pi^{-1}(p)$.

1. **Charts.** Over an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $p$ with regular parameters $x,y$, the
blowup is $\operatorname{Spec}A[y/x]\cup\operatorname{Spec}A[x/y]$ inside $A$-charts, glued by inverting $T$
and $U=T^{-1}$ ([[thm-blowup-smooth-surface-point-charts]]).
2. **Exceptional curve.** $E\cong\mathbb P^1_k$ is an effective Cartier divisor on the regular surface $S'$,
$\mathcal O_E(E)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1_k}(-1)$ and, if $S$ is projective over $k$, $E\cdot E=-1$
([[thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular]], [[lem-exceptional-curve-normal-bundle-minus-one]],
[[lem-blowup-intersection-matrix-at-smooth-point]]). Hence $E$ is an exceptional curve of the first kind and
$\pi$ is a contraction of $E$ ([[lem-blowing-up-a-regular-point-is-a-contraction]]).
3. **One-step factorization.** If $S$ is projective over $k$, then $\pi$ is a birational morphism of regular
projective surfaces which is an isomorphism over $S\setminus\{p\}$, so its factorization into point blowups
consists of the single blowup $\pi$ itself ([[lem-blowing-up-a-regular-point-is-a-contraction]]), and no further
blowup is needed.

For comparison, the companion counterexample page records that normalization of a non-normal surface with a
one-dimensional singular locus is not a point blowup, so the contraction language is genuinely restricted to
regular sources.
items.strategy: Parts 1 and 2 collect the published point-blowup dictionary: the two standard charts glue along $A[y/x,y/x^{-1}]$, the exceptional curve is the projectivized normal direction and is Cartier, and its normal bundle is $\mathcal O(-1)$, so on a projective surface its self-intersection is $\deg_k\mathcal O(-1)=-1$. Part 3 is the definition of the factorization plus the fact that the blowup is an isomorphism off the center. No new claim beyond the published suppliers is made.
